To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) in the lung of the young rat, the specific radioactivity of leucine acetylated to tRNA is in rapid equilibrium with that of free leucyl-t-RNA and 2) the specific radioactivities and fractional synthesis rates of procollagen III, procollagen I are in rapid equilibrium with those of leucyl tRNA

leucine acylation to tRNA in the lung was in equilibrium with the leucine pool in plasma, that the specific radioactivity of leucine acetylated to tRNA was the same as free serum leuine, that the rate of synthesis of total lung protein in vivo was 6.7-15.0 mumoles

the specific radioactivities in vivo of free leucyl-t-RNA in the lungs and leucine incorporated into procollagen I in the lungs of young male rats are in rapid equilibrium with free leucine present in the plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of proteins in the lung.
protein metabolism in rat lung.
the measurement of protein synthesis in rat lungs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate of synthesis of procollagen is a measure of protein synthesis in the lung and is a valid index of the rate of protein synthesis in vivo.

, in young male rats, leucine incorporation into procollagen I is in rapid equilibrium with serum leucine, and that the fractional synthesis rate of procollagen in rat lung is 9%/h, which is similar to the rate for total lung protein.
the specific radioactivity of procollagen III was always lower than that of procollagen and total protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of protein synthesis in the lung is high, but the half-life of proteins synthesized is short, and that the rate of synthesis of the major structural proteins, collagen I and III, is high.

the specific radioactivities in vivo of leucine acetylated to tRNA in the lungs of unanaesthesized young male rats and the rate of incorporation of leucyl-[3H]leukine into mixed proteins are useful parameters for assessing protein synthesis.

the specific radioactivities and fractional synthesis rates of leucine incorporated into procollagen I were equal to those for total lung proteins, indicating that the synthesis of procollagen and other proteins in lung tissue is a reflection of the rate of total protein synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of synthesis of proteins in the lung can be measured in vivo by the use of short (30 min) infusions of radiolabel followed by rapid removal of the lungs.

the specific radioactivities (S.R.s) of free leucines in plasma and leucyl-transfer ribonucleic acid (tRNA) isolated from total lung are in rapid equilibrium with each other, and that the S.R. of leucine acetylated to tRNA is equal to the S.R. for leucine in rapidly turning-over procolla gen I.

the specific radioactivity of leucine acetylated to tRNA in the lung is equal to that in serum, and that the specific radioactivities in procollagen III, procollagen I or total protein are equal to that of leucyltRNA.
